retention.stated: Not published. Tencent has left Weiyun on minimal maintenance

egress.terms: Member-gated speed, with free downloads heavily throttled

tooling: the OpenList weiyun driver, which is cookie-based; github.com/billzhong/weiyun scrapes the share page and then wgets. No rclone backend
chaining: Nothing to chain. A QQ or WeChat account is required, which is +86-gated in practice, and the share endpoints answer with a null body to an unauthenticated caller

limits.value: 10 GB is the free tier total, which is the cap in practice
need_pwd=1 shares require the password before any listing, and the CGI endpoint wants a signed request

reliability_note: The share page ships the share record in a JavaScript blob, so the metadata is embedded and public, and the CGI then answers ret 102027 with a null body. Tencent has left the product on minimal maintenance and the old scrapers work only where the markup has not changed

evidence.proved: returned HTML and not JSON, so the endpoint does not exist

binding_note: 10 GB is 2% of the filter, and the share path is closed to an unauthenticated caller even for metadata. Either number closes it; the quota is the one a reader can check without an account.
notes: The metadata-embedded-in-the-page pattern is worth recording because it is the third variant of the anonymous-read finding: Baidu exposes metadata through an API and refuses the bytes, Weiyun embeds metadata in HTML and refuses the API. Both prove the tree is public and the payload is not.

extras.anonymous_read: metadata embedded in the page, API refused
